title: People Ops Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standard processes for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended as the single source-of-truth for people managers and recruiting partners to ensure a consistent, inclusive, and scalable employee lifecycle.

Scope: Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors (when specified), hiring managers, and interviewers across engineering, product, go-to-market, and support teams.

Key objectives
- Shorten time-to-hire while maintaining quality and inclusiveness.
- Ensure a predictable, psychologically safe and productive first 90 days for new hires.
- Create a repeatable, transparent performance and calibration process tied to growth and compensation cycles.
- Equip managers with checklists, templates, and escalation paths.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

1.1 Recruiting intake and role definition
- Owner: hiring manager (HM) + people-ops recruiter.
- Steps:
  1. HM completes a Role Intake Form (template link) that includes: team mission, outcomes in 90/180/365 days, must-have skills, nice-to-have skills, level and compensation band, relocation/remote constraints, and interview panel requirements.
  2. People-ops reviews job leveling and recommended comp band. Recruiter drafts job posting and sources channels.

1.2 Sourcing and screening
- Channels: internal referrals, LinkedIn Recruiter, campus pipelines, partner job boards, diversity pipelines, agency (only with approval).
- Initial screen (30 min): recruiter conducts phone/VC screen to verify role fit, compensation band alignment and basic eligibility. Recruiters record notes in the Applicant Tracking System (ATS). Target: screen 4–6 candidates per open role per week.

1.3 Interview loop and rubric
- Standard interview stages (example for engineering):
  - Technical screen (45–60 min): algorithmic or system-design mini-coding exercise.
  - Team deep-dive (60 min): architecture, past projects, collaboration and ownership.
  - Manager interview (45 min): role expectations, roadmap, culture fit.
  - Onsite / virtual onsite (3–4 interviews) including cross-functional partner.
- Rubric: Each interviewer scores on a 1–5 scale across core dimensions (technical ability, problem solving, communication, ownership, role-specific skills). Interviewer guidance: use behavioral examples, limit closed questions, and document evidence.
- Hiring signal threshold: average interviewer score >= 3.5 and no critical 'red flag' comments. Final hiring decision requires HM + recruiter sign-off.

1.4 Offer and negotiation
- Offer owner: recruiter + finance for comp approvals.
- Standard offer contains: base salary, equity grant (if applicable), signing bonus (rare, requires approval), benefits summary, start date, and contingency clauses.
- Negotiation guidelines: follow published bands; escalate exceptions (>10% band deviation or unusual equity) to VP People and Finance.

1.5 Time targets and metrics
- Target time-to-offer: 28 calendar days from role open to offer accepted for high-volume roles; 42 days for senior/leadership roles.
- Target acceptance rate: >= 65% for offers extended.
- Diversity target: maintain representation goals in interview pipeline; minimum 30% underrepresented candidates in final onsite slate for senior roles.

2) Candidate experience and compliance

- Communication SLOs: recruiter or HM must acknowledge every applicant within 3 business days.
- Interview accommodations: candidates can request accommodations; recruiter will coordinate with people-ops.
- Background checks and I-9: initiated after offer acceptance. Start date contingent on completion of required checks.

3) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)

3.1 Preboarding (between offer acceptance and start date)
- Owners: recruiter (logistics), IT (accounts & hardware), HM (team onboarding plan).
- Tasks (to complete 5 business days before start):
  - IT provisions laptop, MDM profile, accounts (email, Slack, Jira, internal docs).
  - People-ops sends welcome packet with benefits enrollment, company handbook, and first-day agenda.
  - HM shares first-week schedule and 30/60/90 day plan.
- Example checklist table:
  | Task | Owner | Target | Status |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Laptop order | IT | >= 10 business days pre-start | Required |
  | Accounts created | IT | 3 business days pre-start | Required |
  | First-week schedule shared | HM | 5 business days pre-start | Required |

3.2 Day 0–7: Orientation and basics
- Company orientation (half-day) run by people-ops: benefits, payroll, security training, values & culture.
- Manager onboarding meeting: 1:1 to review role expectations, initial project, key stakeholders, and success metrics.
- Team introductions, pairing buddy assignment (buddy = peer for first 90 days).

3.3 30-day milestone
- Focus: achieve context and early contributions.
- Manager checklist:
  - Confirm access to all required systems.
  - Assign a small, scoped task with clear acceptance criteria.
  - Weekly 1:1s scheduled; set preferred feedback cadence.
  - Provide intro to product, roadmap, and team codebase.
- Expected outcomes: completed onboarding task, initial notes/doc contributions, established working relationships.

3.4 60-day milestone
- Focus: deeper ownership and broader context.
- Expectations: owner of a small feature or operational area; participates in cross-functional planning.

3.5 90-day milestone and calibration
- Manager completes a 90-day review: written summary, candidate self-assessment, and buddy feedback.
- Calibration: people-ops runs a rolling 90-day calibration meeting for new hires in the same quarter to identify systematic onboarding blockers.

4) Performance and feedback cycles

4.1 Cadence and types of feedback
- Continuous feedback: weekly 1:1s with manager (recommended 30–60 min).
- Quarterly check-ins: informal goal review and development planning.
- Annual performance review: formal evaluation tied to compensation and promotion cycles; includes self-assessment, manager assessment, and calibration.

4.2 Rating scale and criteria
- Rating numeric scale: Exceeds Expectations (5), Strong Contributor (4), Meets Expectations (3), Needs Improvement (2), Unsatisfactory (1).
- Core dimensions evaluated: work quality, impact, collaboration, ownership, leadership (for senior levels), and role-specific competencies.

4.3 Promotion and leveling
- Promotions require a dossier: manager write-up, peer feedback, representative work artifacts, and manager + director approval.
- Promotion cycle: rolling but managers are encouraged to align major promotions to quarterly calibration windows for salary budget adjustments.

4.4 Performance improvement plan (PIP)
- Trigger criteria: sustained rating <= 2 across two consecutive check-ins, or clear performance regressions with documented coaching.
- PIP process:
  1. Manager + HR drafts a 60–90 day plan with clear objectives, measurable outcomes, support resources, and check-in cadence.
  2. Expectations and consequences documented; HR reviews for fairness and consistency.
  3. At conclusion, outcomes documented and next steps decided (improvement, role change, or separation).

4.5 Calibration and compensation
- Calibration meetings happen quarterly per function. Managers present evidence for ratings and raises. People-ops facilitates to ensure fairness and budget compliance.
- Compensation approvals: Manager -> Director -> VP People + Finance sign-off for raises outside band or above thresholds.

5) Manager responsibilities and playbooks

5.1 Core manager responsibilities
- Hiring: partner with recruiting to define role, interview, and close offers.
- Onboarding: create 30/60/90 plan and run regular check-ins.
- Development: run career conversations, support learning budgets, and provide promotion guidance.
- Performance management: coach continuously, run check-ins, and participate in calibration.
- Culture & inclusion: ensure psychological safety, equitable task assignment, and unbiased performance assessments.

5.2 New manager checklist (first 30 days as manager)
- Complete Manager Essentials training (people-ops).
- Meet with HR business partner for team composition and compensation overview.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s with each direct report.
- Review current objectives, ongoing projects, and team blockers.

5.3 Practical coaching tips
- Use Specific-Behavior-Impact (SBI) for feedback: describe the specific behavior, explain the impact, and suggest the next step.
- Balance positive reinforcement with timely course-correcting feedback.
- Document feedback summaries in the private manager notes repository.

6) Templates and artifacts (examples)

6.1 Offer email template (excerpt)
``
Subject: Offer from Redwood Inference — [Role]
Hi [Candidate],
We're excited to offer you the role of [Role] at Redwood Inference. Attached is the formal offer letter which outlines base salary, equity, benefits, and start date. Please let us know if you have questions and by when you'd like to accept.
Best,
[Recruiter Name]
``

6.2 30/60/90 day plan template (bullet list)
- 30 days: learn systems, complete onboarding task, meet key stakeholders.
- 60 days: deliver first scoped feature/owner component; present learnings.
- 90 days: lead a cross-team effort or own a measurable area.

6.3 Sample 90-day review form (fields)
- Self assessment (strengths, challenges, impact).
- Manager assessment (progress vs. expectations).
- Buddy feedback.
- Development goals for next 6 months.

7) Escalations & exception handling

- Hiring exceptions: roles with non-standard comp or agency use require VP People approval.
- Onboarding failures (e.g., missing access after 10 business days): HM escalates to IT manager and people-ops; track in the onboarding tracker with SLA target 48 hours for resolution.
- Performance disputes: employee may request HR review; HR facilitates re-evaluation and documents outcome.

8) Metrics and continuous improvement

People-ops tracks the following KPIs monthly: time-to-fill, time-to-offer, offer acceptance rate, new hire retention @ 90/180 days, hiring source effectiveness, and diversity of pipeline. Quarterly review: run retrospective with recruiting, engineering managers, and people-ops to iterate on process improvements.

9) Related pages and references
- people-ops-hiring-onboarding-and-performance-guide-2026 (confluence link)
- interview-rubric-and-guide-2025 (confluence link)
- manager-essentials-training (learning link)

Appendix: Legal & compliance notes

- All offers follow local employment law; people-ops coordinates with Legal for cross-border hires.
- Data retention: candidate assessments retained in ATS for up to 24 months unless candidate requests removal (per privacy policy).

Document maintenance

- Owner: Head of People Operations (people-ops).
- Review cadence: annual review or earlier when major policy changes occur.

If you have questions or need the templates referenced in this playbook, contact people-ops@redwood.com or open a request via the HR portal.
